201: B is correct because Amazon Pinpoint is purpose-built for targeted, two-way SMS messaging with mobile app users, so it can send the confirmation messages and receive user replies. A Pinpoint journey orchestrates the message flow, and streaming Pinpoint events into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams lets the company capture, analyze, and archive the SMS responses durably for the required year.
202: A is correct because SSE-S3 encrypts data at rest by default and AWS manages the encryption keys entirely, rotating them automatically on AWS's schedule without any customer action. This provides the required at-rest encryption and annual key rotation with the least operational overhead compared to customer managed KMS keys.
203: D is correct because the reported delay is caused by the order of the bottleneck: the application that sends meeting invitations cannot keep up with the volume of messages in the SQS queue. An Auto Scaling group that scales based on the depth of the SQS queue (such as the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric) adds capacity exactly when the backlog grows, resolving the late invitations without disrupting the rest of the architecture.
204: C is correct because AWS Lake Formation is designed to build a centralized data lake across S3 and relational sources and provides fine-grained, column- and row-level access controls in one place. Creating a Glue JDBC connection to RDS and registering the S3 bucket in Lake Formation makes both datasets available for analytics with Lake Formation managing permissions, minimizing operational overhead compared to moving or copying the data.
205: C is correct because an S3 bucket is a highly available, durable, and inexpensive origin for static website content behind CloudFront, and using an origin access identity with a bucket policy keeps the content private to CloudFront. This serverless origin removes the need to run or patch any web server, making it the most cost-effective and resilient choice for infrequently updated static documents.
206: C is correct because an EventBridge rule matching the EC2 CreateImage API call captures the event in near real time and can directly target an SNS topic to send the alert. This fully managed, event-driven approach requires no servers, log parsing, or polling, giving the least operational overhead.
207: D is correct because an SQS queue placed between the request intake and DynamoDB buffers writes so that bursts of user requests are retained durably in the queue instead of being dropped when DynamoDB throughput is exhausted. Lambda then drains the queue at a rate DynamoDB can sustain, eliminating lost requests without impacting existing users or requiring more provisioned capacity.
208: A is correct because an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 brings a private IP address for the S3 API into the instance's subnet, so all API calls and data travel over the AWS internal network and never traverse the public internet. Attaching an S3 bucket resource policy that allows only the EC2 instance's IAM role ensures that only that instance can upload data.
209: A is correct because Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) provides an external, shared, in-memory session store that any instance behind the ALB can read or write, which is exactly what distributed session data management requires when instances scale up and down across Availability Zones. Sticky sessions bind users to a single instance and fail when that instance is terminated, whereas Session Manager and STS are unrelated to application user sessions.
210: D is correct because SQS queues durably decouple order collection from order fulfillment, so no data is lost during scaling events even though fulfillment takes longer. Scaling the Auto Scaling groups on a backlog-per-instance metric (queue depth divided by instance count) sizes capacity to the actual outstanding work, optimizing resource utilization during peak traffic rather than over-provisioning to peak values.
211: D is correct because the AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor can search for resources across all Regions and across all supported services in a single query based on the application tag. This is the quickest way to identify every tagged component without writing CLI scripts or per-service queries.
212: A is correct because S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically monitors the objects' access patterns and moves data between frequent and infrequent access tiers with no retrieval fees and no operational management. Since the access pattern is variable and changes rapidly but the data must remain immediately available for up to 3 months, Intelligent-Tiering delivers the lowest cost without increasing retrieval time.
213: A is correct because AWS WAF is a managed web application firewall that inspects HTTP/HTTPS requests and blocks common application-level attacks such as cross-site scripting and SQL injection when its rules are associated with the ALB. It is fully managed by AWS, requires no servers to patch or maintain, and directly reduces the company's operational responsibility.
214: B is correct because AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service where a crawler discovers the CSV data and a Glue ETL job converts it to Apache Parquet with built-in transformations, simply pointing the output at the transformed data bucket. This requires far less development effort than writing custom Spark applications, Bash jobs, or Lambda code.
215: A is correct because transferring 700 TB over a 500 Mbps connection would take far longer than the one-month deadline, so an AWS Snowball device physically moves the data into Amazon S3 quickly. Transitioning the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a lifecycle policy provides the lowest-cost storage for infrequently accessed data retained for seven years.
216: B is correct because enabling default encryption covers all objects added to the bucket in the future, while S3 Inventory lists the existing unencrypted objects and a single S3 Batch Operations copy job applies encryption to millions of existing objects in place. This approach requires the least effort because it is fully managed and avoids re-uploading data or modifying objects one at a time.
217: A is correct because an active-passive Route 53 failover with the required infrastructure elements pre-deployed (a pilot-light style standby) meets the 30-minute downtime tolerance while incurring minimal cost, since the standby does not serve load while the primary is healthy. An Aurora Replica in the second Region provides continuous replication, keeping potential data loss within the accepted window.
218: A is correct because security groups are stateful, so a single inbound rule allowing TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 automatically permits the return traffic without any outbound rule. E is correct because network ACLs are stateless, so the modified NACL that blocks all traffic must explicitly allow inbound TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 plus outbound ephemeral ports 32768-65535 so that responses to the inbound HTTPS requests can return to clients.
219: D is correct because the application is stateful with in-memory tasks, and R5 instances are memory-optimized EC2 instances that directly address the memory pressure causing the performance degradation. Deploying the CloudWatch agent generates the custom application latency and memory metrics needed for future capacity planning since EC2 memory metrics are not provided by default, and making the changes in CloudFormation keeps the management operationally efficient as infrastructure as code.
220: B is correct because AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that scales instantly, charges only for actual invocation time, and costs nothing during the long idle periods when no requests arrive. This matches the highly variable, sporadic request pattern while still completing the asynchronous processing within a few seconds, unlike container services that incur continuous cluster costs.
